Before you watch this, be aware that nearly the entire film tells OJs family life (childhood and both marriages) through flashbacks while he's talking to Bob Shapiro, culminating with the Bronco chase as the film's climax. The movie is more of a biopic/romantic drama than anything else. Some memorable scenes are when OJ finds out about the drowning death of his 2 year old daughter, and OJ punching Nicole for the first time.

The casting in this movie is really good based on sheer physical appearance alone. The actor playing OJ has a large head and a straight, receding hairline, which I always found to be one of OJs most distinctive physical traits (indeed, OJ required custom football helmets because his head was so unusually large). Nicole Simpson and Bob Shapiro are similarly well cast.

The acting is actually not bad, even though I can't shake off the feeling that everyone is articulating almost too perfectly - I keep catching whiffs of that vague transatlantic accent that stage actors have.

The writing's cheesy. There's no way to get around that. Despite American Crime Story being campy and very talkative at times, it at least always feels important, focusing on racism, sexism, fame, money, etc,... This movie focuses primarily on OJ's troubled search for happiness, friendship, love, a sense of himself. Those themes have potential, abstractly speaking, but the end product feels too self-indulgent for me. I don't want to watch one unstable man lie, cry, and fight for an hour and a half.
